text: Hello, I'm Joo, the sprite artist at Dallex. This is Sprite Studio.
heard: Hello, I'm Ju, the sprite artist at Daleks. This is Sprite Studio.

text: It's my squared paper, on the one two eight K Spectrum.
heard: It's my squared paper on the 128k spectrum.

text: Press two for the keys. Q, A, O and P move the cursor.
heard: Press 2 for the keys. Q, A, O and P move the cursor.

text: Press space to paint a square. Hold it and move to draw a line.
heard: Press space to paint a square, hold it and move to draw a line.

text: The pictures at the top show it at true size, as a player sees it.
heard: The pictures at the top show it at true size as a player sees it.

text: And the numbers beside each row are that row's two bytes, in hex.
heard: and the numbers beside each row are that row's two bytes in hex.

text: Press nought for the Lessons, from my drawing chapter.
heard: Press 0 for the lessons from my drawing chapter.

text: Lesson one. A figure is just rows of dots.
heard: Lesson 1. A figure is just rows of dots.

text: Every square is one bit: inked is a one, empty is a zero.
heard: Every square is one bit. Inked is a 1, empty is a 0.

text: Eight squares make a byte, so a row of sixteen is two bytes.
heard: Eight squares make a byte, so a row of sixteen is two bytes.

text: Read a byte from the left. Its squares are worth one hundred and twenty-eight,
heard: Read a byte from the left. Its squares are worth 128.

text: then sixty-four, thirty-two, sixteen, eight, four, two and one.
heard: then 64 32 16 8 4 2 and 1

text: On row one of the Mower, squares two and four are inked.
heard: On row one of the mower, squares two and four are inked.

text: They're worth thirty-two and eight. Add them up, and you get forty.
heard: They're worth 32 and 8. Add them up and you get 40.

text: In hex, forty is two sixteens and eight, so it's written two eight.
heard: in hex. Forty is two sixteens and eight, so it's written two eight.

text: The right half of the row is empty, so that byte is zero zero.
heard: The right half of the row is empty, so that byte is zero, zero.

text: Now I'll ink the very last square, worth one. Watch the right byte.
heard: Now I'll ink the very last square, worth one. Watch the right bite.

text: It reads zero one. You can read any sprite this way, a row at a time.
heard: It reads 01. You can read any sprite this way, a row at a time.

text: Lesson two. Tracing paper shows the last frame as little rings.
heard: Lesson 2. Tracing paper shows the last frame as little rings.

text: A moving figure is just a few pictures, shown one after another.
heard: A moving figure is just a few pictures shown one after another.

text: The Mower's two frames differ in only four rows, at its corners.
heard: The mower's two frames differ in only four rows, at its corners.

text: And the flip book plays both frames, at the speed the game uses.
heard: and the flipbook plays both frames at the speed the game uses.

text: Each picture stays up for four TV frames: nought point nought eight seconds.
heard: Each picture stays up for 4 TV frames, 0.08 seconds.

text: Lesson four, the mask. It clears the scenery under the figure.
heard: Lesson 4: The mask. It clears the scenery under the figure.

text: The Ring mask adds one dot all round the ink. F changes it.
heard: The ring mask adds one dot all round the ink. F changes it.

text: The hatched squares are covered: the ink, the paper inside, and a ring.
heard: The hatched squares are covered, the ink, the paper inside and a ring.

text: Shape has no ring. Box covers the whole box.
heard: Shape has no ring. Box covers the whole box.

text: Lesson three. The Test Ground puts it down three ways.
heard: Lesson three. The test ground puts it down three ways.

text: Copy wipes out the grass in its box. Mix lets the grass show through.
heard: Copy wipes out the grass in its box. Mix lets the grass show through.

text: That's quick, but in busy grass the figure gets hard to see.
heard: That's quick, but in busy grass the figure gets hard to see.

text: Mask then mix clears the grass under the mask, then adds the ink.
heard: Mask then mix clears the grass under the mask Then adds the ink

text: The figure stays solid, with the grass right up to its edge.
heard: The figure stays solid, with the grass right up to its edge.

text: Lesson five. Why does drawing flicker?
heard: Lesson 5. Why does drawing flicker?

text: The top copy rubs the figure out, then draws it again.
heard: The top copy rubs the figure out, then draws it again.

text: Watch it blink. For a moment there's only grass.
heard: Watch it blink. For a moment there's only grass.

text: Draw once changes each dot just once, and never shows the gap.
heard: Draw once changes each dot just once and never shows the gap.

text: So never rub out and redraw. Change each dot straight to its new value.
heard: So never rub out and redraw. Change each dot straight to its new value.

text: Lesson six. On the Spectrum, colour belongs to the cell.
heard: Lesson 6. On the spectrum, colour belongs to the cell.

text: The screen is cut into blocks, eight dots square.
heard: The screen is cut into blocks eight dots square.

text: Each block has one ink colour and one paper colour. Clashing blocks flash.
heard: Each block has one ink colour and one paper colour. Clashing blocks flash.

text: In Ink mode, every block the Mower touches takes its red ink.
heard: In Ink mode, every block the mower touches takes its red ink.

text: But the grass in those blocks is ink too, so it turns red as well.
heard: but the grass in those blocks is inked too, so it turns red as well.

text: One dot off the grid, the Mower touches nine blocks instead of four.
heard: One dot off the grid, the mower touches nine blocks instead of four.

text: That frame's wrong. Look. The grass round the Mower has turned red.
heard: That frame's wrong. Look, the grass round the mower has turned red.

text: Press nine for the Sheet. It holds up to eight figures.
heard: Press 9 for the sheet. It holds up to 8 figures.

text: The data size counts the Row Codes a game would store.
heard: The data size counts the row codes a game would store.

text: A game often stores a figure eight times, shifted one dot further each time.
heard: A game often stores a figure eight times, shifted one dot further each time.

text: Shifting it right spills into the next byte, so each row needs three bytes.
heard: Shifting it right spills into the next byte, so each row needs three bytes.

text: Two frames, eight positions, sixteen rows, three bytes: seven hundred and sixty-eight.
heard: two frames, eight positions, 16 rows, three bytes, 768.

text: Stored once, it's two frames, sixteen rows, two bytes: just sixty-four.
heard: Stored once, it's 2 frames, 16 rows, 2 bytes, just 64.

text: S saves the sheet to tape. X exports the figure, ready for a game.
heard: S saves the sheet to tape. X exports the figure, ready for a game.

text: Now draw something, flip it, and show me. I'll find your stray pixel.
